Run 1 refuses attributably at doc-sync with `git rev-parse` asserting tip EXACTLY A; a plain retry meets the IDENTICAL doc-sync gate (the #186 assertion, which my ask did not even demand); run 2 with --allow-doc-skew converges (BeadClosed, bead ancestor of spec branch, marker cleared). Verified green.

Minor residual, non-blocking: no complete-level assertion pins that Run passes the FORMATTED subject (TestRun_AutoCommitMaterializesViaSnapshot inspects Args[0]/Args[3] but not the subject Args[4]) — reverting the materializationSubject call site to "" would stay green today. A one-line assertion would close it; fold into any later round or a follow-up, not worth a round by itself.

New anchors pinned (TestADR0041G1DeliveredOrdering-style additions in adr0041_amendment_test.go) plus a red-on-revert for the removed check-after-D-only sentence — I verified that pinned stale string is the exact §1 sentence the diff removed. ask_classifications.ask_5_unknown_stage_closure: ADDRESSED — isKnownStage closes the discriminator over {materialization, artifact-sync}; unknown, empty, AND (beyond my ask) duplicate-trailer encodings all take the foreign-clear path (gitutil.ReadStageTrailer now reports any non-exactly-one trailer count as absent — ambiguity is never resolved by picking one); the clear is CAS'd against the observed OID (G4), so the cleanup itself cannot destroy a racing invocation's newer evidence. runMaterialization's else-catchall is now reachable only with artifact-sync since the closed discriminator is the sole resumeStage producer. ask_classifications.ask_6_error_propagation: ADDRESSED — all three previously-swallowed reads now propagate, one more than my ask named: the S-stage pre-publish ReadStageMarker error (was: silent CREATE degrade), the discriminator's oid^ parent-resolution error (was: silent FOREIGN reclassification that DELETED the marker on a read blip — the evidence-destroying case), and the discriminator's bead-tip RevParseRef error (round-1 code cleared the marker there too; now propagates). Each has an injection test; verified green.

g5_adaptation_judgment: SOUND, and I verified the premise rather than trusting it: internal/panel/gate.go's clause (7) (Req 11) blocks whenever a panel is registered AND the worktree carries uncommitted USER dirt ('would auto-commit them past review'), with artifact paths already exempted — and git log confirms bead 6 did not touch gate.go (last modified by spec 127 work). Since an M-stage build requires exactly such user dirt, and the panel gate runs BEFORE runMaterialization on every non-resume run, an M-stage materialization under a live panel is genuinely unreachable — the run refuses at the panel gate before any snapshot. With no panel registered the gate is fail-open and there is no stale-SHA check to bypass, so R2's literal M-stage-kill-under-live-panel scenario is structurally vacuous in both directions. The property actually under test — Run's resumeStage!="" guard skips the panel gate — is stage-agnostic (the guard tests non-emptiness, not stage identity), so leg xxii's S-stage-advance kill proves the identical guard the M-stage version would have. The unreachability argument IS stated, in leg xxii's own comment block, which I consider adequate disposition; echoing one sentence into ADR-0041 §3(i) would be a nice-to-have, not an ask. One adversarial variant I checked and am satisfied by: a fail-open (no-panel) run killed after an M-advance, with a panel registered before the re-run, WILL resume past the new panel's gate — but that is the protocol's designed marker-proves-gates-passed semantics (the original run's gate outcome, fail-open Allow, was durable), not a laundering hole: the marker only exists because every gate of the publishing run passed.
